A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LaVR, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V1's supplementary page was inspected and matched against v2's main text; v2 contains no appended supplement.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation comparisons, cycle-consistency and pose-reconstruction measurements, and adapter ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and reports conditioning ablations and a qualitative 4D reconstruction comparison in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Figure 4 remove v1's channel-wise grouping of m consecutive frames, changing the conditioning sequence from T/(mk) groups to T/k feature maps. V2 instead describes spatial-query attention followed by channel projection. This substantially revises the reported adapter procedure, while the CUT3R/DiT framework, pose conditioning and training loss remain.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MultiCamVideo and evaluate novel video trajectories using 100 dynamic Pexels videos and 50 static DL3DV videos. The added reconstruction analysis examines generated videos without establishing new dataset coverage or input scenarios.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain Gen3C, TrajectoryCrafter and ReCamMaster. The new Figure 10 uses ReCamMaster and TrajectoryCrafter, but introduces no new competing method and does not remove a comparator from an existing comparison.

E3.justification: The main training budget, evaluation sample counts, 33-frame preprocessing, 480×832 resolution, four trajectories and metrics remain unchanged. The replacement ablation introduces latent/pose removal controls instead of fixed-computation k/m configurations, and Figure 10 adds qualitative inspection of BA-Track point-cloud reconstructions.

E4.justification: V1's compression-parameter sensitivity study is removed and replaced by an ablation separating the contributions of CUT3R latents and source poses. V2 also adds a reconstructed-geometry case study in Section 4.2 and Figure 10, substantially changing the questions addressed by the supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The statistical reporting practice for retained measurements is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 5 retain their results. Table 3 replaces the k/m sensitivity rows with conditioning results, including cycle PSNR 17.90 without CUT3R latents and 20.70 without source poses. Figure 10 adds qualitative reconstruction evidence, and Figure 6 corrects its description of ReCamMaster's top-row failure.

T1.justification: The formal state-token definition and conditional flow-matching objective remain unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations; the revised adapter tensor layouts describe the procedural change assessed under M1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: LRM latent conditioning, a lightweight adapter, and improved geometric consistency and visual quality over geometrically conditioned and unconditioned baselines. The new analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its new ablation as showing that latent conditioning supplies the principal benefit and source poses play a complementary role. It also discusses ambiguity in geometric ground truth and explicitly lists conditioning overhead as a limitation. The transparent-object limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 specifies 512-dimensional query/token embeddings and pose-adapter injection into each DiT block. It omits v1's two-layer, 12-head decoder specification, uncompressed-iteration timing, and supplementary dataset details of 136K Unreal Engine 5 scenes with ten synchronized videos each. Model-size information moves into the main text; hardware, training budget, learning rates and project access information remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds eight bibliography entries, including 2D Gaussian Splatting, Marigold, Customize-a-Video and Mip-Splatting, mainly expanding citations within existing related-work paragraphs. Its positioning between explicit geometric conditioning and geometrically unconditioned generation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 is rewritten, experimental subsections are reorganized, and supplementary model-size information moves into the main text. Grammar, terminology, affiliation and acknowledgements receive edits. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn, Figure 3 receives label and connection updates, Table 3 changes its row structure, and Figure 10 is added. Figure 6's caption is corrected. Existing qualitative image panels, Figure 5 and Tables 1–2 are retained, with localized formatting and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new Table 3 directly tests whether gains arise from scene latents or source poses, strengthening support for the central contribution. Figure 10 and the clearer adapter explanation add useful evidence and clarity. These gains are limited by removal of the compression sensitivity study and some dataset and implementation details. The unchanged main benchmark scores do not establish a performance improvement.
